title: People / recruiter scoring shortlist
notes: Seeded from Method Lab frontier screen (2026-07-26): 1944 unique arXiv papers, 686 relevant, top 10 + honorable mentions for scoring people with rubrics (recruiting + adjacent). Drop this file into simple-papers data/digests/.

papers.title: From Rubrics to Reliable Scores: Evidence-Grounded Text Evaluation with LLM Judges
papers.summary: RULERS compiles natural-language rubrics into executable, versioned criteria with evidence checks and scale calibration for reliable LLM judging.
papers.summarySimple: Turns scoring rubrics into executable checklists so AI judges score more like careful humans.

impact.forTech: Build a rubric compiler + evidence-anchored scorer that versions criteria, verifies cited evidence, and calibrates score scales for hiring scorecards, essay grading, or any analytic rubric.
impact.forBusiness: Selling point: replace one-shot holistic LLM scores with auditable, versioned rubrics recruiters and educators can trust.

papers.title: Beyond the Resumé: A Rubric-Aware Automatic Interview System for Information Elicitation
papers.summary: Open multi-turn interview system that updates calibrated belief over rubric-oriented candidate KSAs instead of one-shot resume scores.
papers.summarySimple: An AI interviewer that fills a job rubric by asking better questions and updating confidence as answers come in.

impact.forTech: Ship a recruiter interview desk: role rubrics, belief updates per KSA, calibrated saturation stopping, and exportable score trails with public demo/code.
impact.forBusiness: Early hiring wedge: cheaper than SME interviews, richer than resume screens.

papers.title: Trust or Escalate: LLM Judges with Provable Guarantees for Human Agreement
papers.summary: Selective LLM evaluation with confidence estimation and cascaded escalation that guarantees a target human-agreement level.
papers.summarySimple: Only trust an AI score when it is confident; otherwise escalate to a stronger model or a human.

impact.forTech: Add a selective scoring layer: estimate judge confidence, abstain/escalate under a user-set human-agreement guarantee, cascade cheap→strong judges.
impact.forBusiness: Required reliability control for any product that scores people.

papers.title: CoMAI: A Collaborative Multi-Agent Framework for Robust and Equitable Interview Evaluation
papers.summary: Multi-agent interview framework with question, security, rubric scoring, and summarization agents; validated in admissions.
papers.summarySimple: A team of specialized AI agents runs safer, fairer interviews with rubric scoring instead of one chat bot.

impact.forTech: Implement modular interview agents (question gen, injection defense, rubric score, audit summary) with FSM orchestration for hiring/admissions.
impact.forBusiness: Ports admissions-validated interview scoring to recruiting with security against prompt injection.

papers.title: Autorubric: Unifying Rubric-based LLM Evaluation
papers.summary: Unifies ensemble judging, bias mitigation, and few-shot calibration for rubric-based LLM evaluation into one framework.
papers.summarySimple: A practical toolkit that combines the best tricks for making AI rubric scoring consistent.

impact.forTech: Productize a unified rubric-judge pipeline: criterion decomposition, jury ensembles, bias counters, few-shot calibration, structured outputs.
impact.forBusiness: Platform layer for any scorecard product.

papers.title: Diagnosing the Reliability of LLM-as-a-Judge via Item Response Theory
papers.summary: Applies Item Response Theory to treat LLM judges as measurement instruments and diagnose reliability beyond surface agreement.
papers.summarySimple: Uses exam-design math to check whether an AI scorer is a stable measuring tool, not just often agreeing with humans.

impact.forTech: Add IRT diagnostics for judges/scorecards: item difficulty, judge discrimination, reliability curves before shipping people-scores.
impact.forBusiness: Psychometric credibility for education, hiring, and performance scoring products.

papers.title: Evaluating Scoring Bias in LLM-as-a-Judge
papers.summary: Defines and measures scoring-specific biases: rubric order, score ID labeling, and reference-answer effects.
papers.summarySimple: Shows how tiny prompt/rubric tweaks quietly change AI scores — and how to test for that.

impact.forTech: Ship a scoring-bias audit suite for scorecards: shuffle rubric order, vary score IDs, ablate references; report stability metrics.
impact.forBusiness: Compliance and trust feature for recruiter/HR AI scoring.

papers.title: An Efficient Long-Context Ranking Architecture With Calibrated LLM Distillation: Application to Person-Job Fit
papers.summary: Late cross-attention re-ranker for long multilingual resumes with calibrated distillation for person-job fit.
papers.summarySimple: A fast, calibrated ranking model that matches long resumes to jobs without burning a giant chat model on every candidate.

impact.forTech: Build a calibrated resume↔job re-ranker for long/multilingual CVs with distill-from-LLM teacher scores and production latency.
impact.forBusiness: Screening-at-scale product for recruiters and staffing platforms.

papers.title: Fairness in AI-Driven Recruitment: Challenges, Metrics, Methods, and Future Directions
papers.summary: Survey of bias sources, fairness metrics, and mitigations across sourcing, screening, interviewing, and selection.
papers.summarySimple: A field guide to measuring and fixing unfairness in AI hiring tools end to end.

impact.forTech: Encode hiring-stage fairness checks (demographic parity, equalized odds, impact ratio) into scoring/audit products with stage-aware mitigations.
impact.forBusiness: Operating manual for compliant recruiter scoring products.

papers.title: FAIRE: Assessing Racial and Gender Bias in AI-Driven Resume Evaluations
papers.summary: Benchmark and code for testing racial and gender bias in LLM resume evaluation.
papers.summarySimple: A ready-made test set to audit whether resume-scoring AI treats people differently by race or gender.

impact.forTech: Integrate FAIRE-style resume audit packs into any LLM screener: counterfactual names/demographics, impact-ratio reports, regression tests.
impact.forBusiness: Audit/compliance wedge for AI recruiting vendors and buyers.

papers.title: Prometheus: Inducing Fine-grained Evaluation Capability in Language Models
papers.summary: Open evaluator LM trained for fine-grained, user-defined rubric scoring as an alternative to proprietary judges.
papers.summarySimple: An open AI judge trained to score answers against custom rubrics without needing GPT-4 every time.

impact.forTech: Host an open rubric judge model for offline/private scoring of candidate answers and essays.
impact.forBusiness: Cost and privacy path for rubric scoring at scale.

papers.title: Judging LLM-as-a-Judge with MT-Bench and Chatbot Arena
papers.summary: Foundational LLM-as-judge protocol with MT-Bench and human preference arena; still the comparison baseline.
papers.summarySimple: The classic playbook for using AI models to judge other AI answers, checked against human votes.

impact.forTech: Keep pairwise preference + arena-style human calibration as a baseline lane beside analytic rubric scores.

papers.title: A Survey on LLM-as-a-Judge
papers.summary: Survey taxonomy of LLM-as-a-judge methods, biases, and reliability practices.
papers.summarySimple: A map of how people use AI judges, where they fail, and what actually improves reliability.

impact.forTech: Use as design checklist when building judge pipelines: pointwise vs pairwise, bias classes, meta-eval.
impact.forBusiness: Reduces reinventing known judge failure modes.

papers.title: Fairness and Bias in Algorithmic Hiring: a Multidisciplinary Survey
papers.summary: Multidisciplinary survey of fairness in algorithmic hiring across ML, law, and I-O psychology narratives.
papers.summarySimple: Looks at unfair hiring algorithms from tech, legal, and workplace-psychology angles together.

impact.forTech: Ground hiring-score products in multidisciplinary fairness constraints, not ML metrics alone.
impact.forBusiness: Buyer education and policy alignment for AI recruiting.

papers.title: PReMISE: Policy Rubrics as Measurement Specifications for LLM Judges
papers.summary: Treats policy rubrics as measurement specifications so vague criteria become scoreable, stable judge inputs.
papers.summarySimple: Turns fuzzy policies like “be helpful and fair” into clear, measurable scoring specs for AI judges.

impact.forTech: Add a policy→measurement-spec compiler for scorecards used in hiring, content, and performance review.
impact.forBusiness: Makes company policies into enforceable scoring rules.
